title: SDK: add OTel-friendly hooks (middleware) for request/stream spans
author: Dana Lo
release_notes: - Add middleware-style hooks for request lifecycle instrumentation (suitable for OpenTelemetry). - Provide streaming-friendly callbacks to avoid custom patching in quickstart templates. - Document span naming + attribute recommendations and cardinality guidance.
description: Motivation: Quickstart templates need to attach OpenTelemetry spans/attributes to Redwood SDK calls (including streaming) without monkey-patching fetch or forking the client. This PR introduces a small, explicit middleware/hook surface that lets templates (and customer apps) wrap requests with spans, capture timing, and attach sanitized attributes in a consistent way. Summary of changes: 1) Add a new optional `hooks` config on `RedwoodClient` that supports request lifecycle hooks for both unary and streaming calls. 2) Provide typed hook payloads (request options, model, route, attempt count, request_id when available) with guidance to avoid high-cardinality fields by default. 3) Add streaming callbacks that fire when the stream is opened, per-chunk (optional), and when the stream closes/aborts, so templates can finish spans correctly even on disconnects. 4) Ensure hook execution is safe: hooks are best-effort, isolated from the request path (exceptions are caught and logged at debug), and are not awaited by default except where needed for correct ordering. API details: `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey, hooks: { onRequestStart, onRequestRetry, onResponse, onStreamOpen, onStreamChunk, onStreamClose, onError } })`. Hooks receive a context object with stable fields intended for OTel attributes: `redwood.request_id`, `redwood.model`, `redwood.route`, `http.method`, `http.status_code`, `net.peer.name` (if available), plus duration fields. We intentionally do NOT include prompt/response content or user identifiers. Example (docs snippet included): `const client = new RedwoodClient({ hooks: { onRequestStart: ({ ctx }) => { const span = tracer.startSpan('redwood.chat'); ctx.span = span; span.setAttribute('redwood.model', ctx.model); }, onResponse: ({ ctx, response }) => { ctx.span?.setAttribute('http.status_code', String(response.status)); ctx.span?.end(); }, onError: ({ ctx, error }) => { ctx.span?.recordException(error); ctx.span?.setStatus({ code: 2 }); ctx.span?.end(); } } });` Notes on OTel dependency: The SDK does not take a hard dependency on `@opentelemetry/api`. Hooks are plain functions; templates can wire OTel in their app layer. This keeps the SDK lightweight and avoids version conflicts. Tests: Added unit tests for hook ordering (start -> retry* -> response/error), stream close semantics (normal close vs abort), and ensuring hook exceptions do not fail requests. Also added a small integration-style test using a fake streaming transport to verify `onStreamClose` executes on disconnect. Docs: Updated README + JSDoc with recommended span names and attributes, and a note about cardinality (do not attach `prompt`, `messages`, full URLs with query params, or tool args as attributes).

docs: add instrumentation guidance + examples for quickstarts
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we ensure we don’t encourage high-cardinality attributes? Please call out which fields are safe (model, route, request_id) and which are not (prompt, full URLs with query params, tool args).
Dana Lo (author): Added a dedicated doc section + JSDoc warnings, and constrained the HookContext to only include the sanitized URL origin/path by default (no query).
Ibrahim Khan: Hook ordering looks good for unary requests. For streaming, do we always end the span on disconnect? We’ve seen proxies drop connections and we need spans to close to avoid leaks.
Dana Lo (author): Added `onStreamClose` firing on both normal close and abort; also ensured we call it from the finally path in the streaming iterator wrapper.
Brian Murphy: Please confirm hooks can’t break requests if user code throws. Also, can we expose attempt count for retries so templates can annotate spans?
Dana Lo (author): Hooks are invoked via `safeInvoke` and exceptions are swallowed (debug logged). Added `attempt` and `maxAttempts` to retry callbacks and included tests.
Caleb Johnson: Minor: consider naming `onRequestStart` vs `onRequest`. Either is fine but keep it explicit that it’s per-attempt or per-logical-request.
Dana Lo (author): Kept `onRequestStart` as logical-request start, added `onRequestRetry` per-attempt. Updated docs with a timing diagram.
Allison Grant: Approved after docs update and stream close tests.
Ibrahim Khan: Approved. This unblocks the quickstart templates without patching fetch.
follow_ups: Add a cookbook example in redwood-docs quickstarts showing end-to-end OTel wiring (tracer/provider setup) using these hooks (tracked in ENG-4184).
Consider adding an optional `onSpan` convenience helper in the SDK docs (no SDK API change) to standardize span naming across templates.
